To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radiative power (RP) of an emitter is sensitive to the orientation of the emitter, the dielectric constant (ε) of the substrate, and the distance (d) from the emitter to the interface, as well as the dielectric constant ε of the medium surrounding the emitter.

the radiative power (or radiative decay rate) of an emitter near the dielectric interface is strongly perturbed at less than λ /2π by the boundary conditions on the interface, rather than evanescent waves, when the dielectric constant ( ε ) of the emitter resting medium is larger (or smaller) than that of the dielectric interface.

the radiative power and the radiative lifetime of an emitting dipolar dipole are strongly perturbed at less than λ /2π from the interface, and that the radiative lifetime is sensitive to the dipolar orientation in the proximity (λ/2π) of an interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiative power and radiative decay time of an emitter in the proximity of dielectric interfaces.
the radiative power emitted from an emitter in the proximity of an interface between two dielectrics.
the radiative power emitted by a dipole in close proximity to a dielectric interface, and we consider the case where the dipole is a quantum-dot excitonic transition dipole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radiative power (or the exciton radiative rate) of a dipole is perturbed strongly by the interface when the dielectric constant is large, but the perturbation is small when the dielectric is small.

the radiative power for a dipole in proximity of a dielectricsubstrate interface is perturbed significantly by the interface due the imposed boundary conditions of the plane wave components of the electromagnetic waves, and not the evanescent wave components.

the radiative power for the dipole in the presence of a dielectric substrate can be expressed as a function of the dipole position and orientation, and the dielectric constants of the dipole, substrate and the surrounding media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dipole radiative power is sensitive to the dielectric environment and the orientation of the dipole in the environment, and the dipole radiated power can explain the distance-dependent excitonic lifetime of quantum dots near a dielectric substrate interface.
the radiative power for a dipole near a planar dielectric interface is sensitive to the dielectric constant, the dipole orientation, the dipole position and the wavelength of the emitted light.
we have shown that the radiative power for a dipole in a medium can be calculated by a simple method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the radiative power for a dipole near a planar dielectric interface is strongly perturbed at less than λ /2π due to the imposed conditions on the plane wave, rather than the exponentially decaying evanescent wave.
the radiative power, and hence the lifetime, is not a good measure of the coupling strength between the emitter and the interface.
the radiative power for a dipole is perturbed strongly by the interface at less than λ / 2π, rather than by the evanescent wave.
